concepts.preferred_label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the tonsil
concepts.why: The patient has a history of tobacco use and betel-nut chewing, which are risk factors for tonsil cancer, and a protruding lesion in the right palatine tonsil.
The patient has a history of odynophagia and a persistent sensation of a foreign body in his throat, which could be consistent with a peritonsillar abscess.
The patient has a protruding lesion in the right palatine tonsil, which could be a tonsillar cyst.
The patient has a history of fish bone impaction, which could still be present despite no visible fish bone.
The patient has a history of tobacco use and betel-nut chewing, which are risk factors for oral cavity cancer.
The patient has a history of odynophagia and a persistent sensation of a foreign body in his throat, which could be consistent with tonsil TB.
The patient has a protruding lesion in the right palatine tonsil and no cervical lymphadenopathy, which could be consistent with lymphoma of the tonsil.

The absence of mucosal ulceration or mass elsewhere in the upper aerodigestive tract and the presence of a hard, mobile, well-delineated, nontender, and yellowish-white lesion through the right palatine tonsil suggest a tonsillolith.
